stem: According to lung allocation references, how often is each waitlist candidate's Lung Allocation Score (LAS) updated?

options.text: Every 5 years regardless of clinical change
Only at the time of organ implantation

explanation.rationale_correct: Under the LAS system, each candidate's LAS is updated every 6 months as part of waitlist maintenance.

rationale_incorrect.B: LAS is recalculated periodically during the waiting period, not only at listing.
rationale_incorrect.C: Six-month updates are required, not five-year intervals.
rationale_incorrect.D: LAS updates occur during the waiting period before transplant surgery.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 1, Lung transplantation → LAS implementation → item 5
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Each candidate's LAS is updated every 6 months

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → lung LAS (updated every 6 months); PDF p. 39 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Third lung item; anchor verified on Cupples p. 39.

stem: A heart transplant candidate has a panel reactive antibody (PRA) greater than 10%. Which preoperative coordination step aligns with standard heart transplant protocols?

options.text: Obtain a recipient/donor prospective crossmatch when indicated
Skip all immunologic testing because PRA does not affect transplant planning
List the patient without any viral serology testing
Defer all preoperative laboratory testing until the day of discharge

explanation.rationale_correct: Heart preoperative protocols include laboratory testing and a prospective crossmatch when PRA is greater than 10%, indicating higher risk for unacceptable donor antibodies.

rationale_incorrect.B: Elevated PRA triggers additional immunologic coordination including crossmatch when required.
rationale_incorrect.C: Preoperative protocols include viral serologies and other standard tests.
rationale_incorrect.D: Preoperative tests are obtained in a timely manner before surgery, not deferred until discharge.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 9, Heart Transplantation → Preparation for Surgery → A. Obtain preoperative tests → 2–3
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Recipient/donor prospective crossmatch … if the potential recipient's PRA is >10%

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 9 → Preparation for Surgery → preoperative tests and crossmatch when PRA >10%; PDF p. 410 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Third heart organ item; anchor verified on Cupples p. 410.

stem: A deceased-donor kidney offer is generated for a listed candidate, and the donor is identified as a Public Health Service (PHS) increased-risk donor. What must occur before transplantation proceeds?

options.text: The patient is notified at the time of the organ offer and must consent to proceed
The center may proceed without notifying the candidate because PHS status is confidential
The candidate is automatically removed from the waitlist if PHS risk is identified
PHS increased-risk designation eliminates the need for any organ-offer discussion

explanation.rationale_correct: When a donor is identified as a PHS increased-risk donor, the patient is notified at the time of the organ offer and must consent before proceeding; refusal does not affect waitlist status.

rationale_incorrect.B: PHS increased-risk status requires candidate notification and consent at offer time.
rationale_incorrect.C: Candidates may refuse PHS-risk organs without losing waitlist standing.
rationale_incorrect.D: PHS designation requires explicit offer-time disclosure and consent, not silent proceeding.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → §8. Organ allocation → g.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: the patient is notified at the time of the organ offer and must consent to proceed

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → §8. Organ allocation → g. (PHS increased-risk donor notification and consent); PDF p. 101 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Distinct 020600 angle from cctc-2004/2015; anchor verified on Cupples p. 101.

stem: After evaluation, the interdisciplinary team approves a liver candidate with conditions pending completion of a smoking cessation program. How should this outcome be communicated?

options.text: Inform the patient they are approved as a candidate with specified conditions such as smoking cessation
Tell the patient they are fully listed with no outstanding requirements
Withhold the conditional approval until after transplant surgery
Inform the patient they are permanently ineligible without opportunity to meet conditions

explanation.rationale_correct: Evaluation outcome communication includes informing patients when they are approved as candidates with conditions such as completion of smoking, drug, or alcohol cessation programs.

rationale_incorrect.B: Conditional approval explicitly includes outstanding requirements before full listing implementation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Conditional outcomes are communicated at evaluation conclusion, not deferred until surgery.
rationale_incorrect.D: Conditional approval is distinct from permanent ineligibility.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → §7. Selection criteria and evaluation outcome → c.ii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: approved as a candidate with conditions, such as Completion of smoking, drug and/or alcohol cessation program

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → §7. Selection criteria and evaluation outcome → c.ii. (approved with conditions); PDF p. 100 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Distinct 020400 angle from cctc-2007/2017; seventh liver organ item; anchor verified on Cupples p. 100.
